description:
# ✨ Feature / Enhancement PR

## 🔗 Epic / Issue

Closes #3519

---

## 🚀 Summary

Replaces per-row action buttons across all admin tables with a fixed-positioned overflow menu (first introduced on the Gateways table, then rolled out to Tools, Servers, Resources, Prompts, Agents, and Roots) and extracts the shared Alpine state and scroll-lock logic into a reusable `Admin.overflowMenu()` factory component.

---

## 🧪 Checks

- [X] `make lint` passes
- [X] `make test` passes
- [X] CHANGELOG updated (if user-facing)

---

## 📓 Notes (optional)

- New file: `mcpgateway/admin_ui/components/overflow-menu.js`.
- All seven templates (roots table in `admin.html` + six partials) use `x-data="Admin.overflowMenu('…-table-wrapper')"` instead of ~20 lines of duplicated inline JS.
- The `components/` directory is set up to house future Alpine components.

reviews.author: vishu-bh
reviews.body:
Thanks for the cleanup here. Extracting the repeated overflow-menu behavior into a shared Alpine component is a good direction, and the admin table markup is noticeably easier to follow after this refactor. I did spot a few regressions that look worth addressing before merge:

1. `mcpgateway/templates/agents_partial.html:70`
The new A2A “View” action calls `Admin.viewAgent(...)`, but the JS bundle exposes `Admin.viewA2AAgent` in `mcpgateway/admin_ui/admin.js`. As written, clicking “View” looks like it will throw on the client instead of opening the agent details modal.

2. `mcpgateway/templates/tools_partial.html:86`
`mcpgateway/templates/prompts_partial.html:80`
`mcpgateway/templates/servers_partial.html:103`
`mcpgateway/templates/agents_partial.html:82`
Several migrated activate/deactivate forms now call bare `handleToggleSubmit(...)` instead of `Admin.handleToggleSubmit(...)`. Since the handler is attached to `Admin`, these submits appear to be broken for the affected tables and will likely fail with a `ReferenceError`.

3. `tests/unit/js/overflow-menu.test.js`
The new unit coverage is useful for the shared component itself, but it doesn’t currently cover the template-to-handler wiring where the regressions above were introduced. A small integration-style JS test or a Playwright assertion that actually executes one of these row actions would make this refactor safer.

reviews.author: vishu-bh
reviews.body:
Thanks @gcgoncalves for addressing the comments. Changes looks good to me, there a behavior I observed when clicking the menu item in table, scroll gets locked. So when overflow-menu is visible you cannon scroll the screen. 

I think it should be worth looking into it. Rest all looks good to me.

commits.message:
fix(ui): harden overflow menu — correctness, security, and test coverage

- Replace broken runtime Tailwind class interpolation with :style binding
  across tools, servers, resources, prompts, and roots templates
- Forward wrapperId through Alpine.data registration in events.js
- Add destroy() hook to clear scroll-lock on HTMX swap / row removal
- Add ref guards with console.warn for missing $refs.trigger / $refs.menu
- Add ARIA attributes (aria-haspopup, aria-label, aria-orientation)
- Simplify multi-menu coordination to module-level currentlyOpen variable
- Add x-cloak + CSS rule to prevent pre-Alpine menu flash
- Close overflow menu on form-submit via @submit="menuOpen = false"
- Restore testTool/testPrompt re-entry guards with data-test-*-id hooks
  and escapeAttrValue() defensive CSS selector escaping
- Cap oversized menus with max-height + internal scroll when taller than
  viewport
- Rename _open_action_dropdown to public open_action_dropdown with alias
- Update all Playwright tests to open overflow menu before asserting
  row-action visibility (extended, integration, regression, HTMX tests)
- Add 49 overflow-menu unit tests (destroy, coordination, ref guards,
  tall-menu fallback, zero-rect guard)

Closes #3519
